verdict.rationale: FireHydrant documents internal status pages, ephemeral per-incident pages meant for the internal team only. That covers the employee-only audience, and it ships external status pages (FireHydrant-hosted or Atlassian). However, the docs say internal pages for organization-public incidents require no auth to view, which implies only a coarse public-versus-private incident distinction rather than configurable access control. Nothing shows customer-specific private pages. Missing for 10: customer-specific or audience-segmented private status pages, explicit access-control configuration (SSO/password/allowlist gating), persistent rather than per-incident internal pages, and independent hands-on corroboration.
